name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Ghostwriter is a Java command-line automation and documentation engine in the Machai ecosystem. It scans project repositories, recognizes embedded @guidance directives in supported file types, composes project-aware prompts, and dispatches them to configured GenAI providers. It supports guided file processing for source code, Markdown documentation, HTML/XML content, Python, TypeScript, PlantUML, and standalone @guidance.txt files. It also provides Act mode, where reusable TOML workflows define system instructions, prompt templates, episodes, inheritance, default prompt values, model overrides, path scanning, exclusions, non-recursive execution, concurrency, and interactive chat behavior. Ghostwriter includes host-integrated function tools for file reading and writing, patch application, directory listing, secure command execution with logs, web content retrieval, REST API calls, act execution, guidance-tag discovery, asynchronous processing, project-context variables, and workflow control. Typical use cases include repository-wide documentation generation, Javadoc updates, project site maintenance, code review workflows, automated unit-test generation, vulnerability remediation workflows, SonarQube issue fixing, AI-assisted commits, and CI/CD-friendly guided automation.

usageContext: Interactive AI chat workflows through Acts
Tool-calling workflows for local files, commands, web APIs, acts, and project context
integrations: GenAI providers configured through Machai genai-client

constructors.description: Creates a processor that runs Ghostwriter in Act mode. The projectDir is the project root used for relative paths, genai identifies the AI provider or model, and configurator supplies runtime properties. Acts can be loaded from bundled resources, a configured local or remote acts location, or an absolute TOML file path.

examples.description: Creates an Act processor, configures a custom acts directory, and loads the generic task act with a user prompt. The act may then be executed against a project layout.

constructors.description: Creates a processor that scans a project tree for embedded @guidance directives and dispatches extracted guidance to a configured GenAI provider. It supports single-module and multi-module project layouts and uses format-specific reviewers for supported file types.

examples.description: Creates a guidance processor for the current project root. The processor can be configured with scan paths and then used to process files containing guidance tags.

constructors.description: Creates the base AI file processor used by Ghostwriter workflows. It prepares prompts, resolves included prompt fragments, applies YAML front matter input parameters, publishes per-file process metadata, and optionally supports interactive processing.

examples.description: Creates a base AI file processor with a default prompt for non-interactive project processing.

features.name: Ghostwriter CLI entry point
features.signature: public static void org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter.main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.io.IOException, org.apache.commons.cli.ParseException
features.description: Starts the Ghostwriter command-line application. The CLI accepts a scan target path or pattern and options for project directory, threads, model, instructions, exclusions, input logging, acts location, and Act mode. It supports raw paths, glob patterns, and regex patterns for repository scanning.

examples.description: Runs Ghostwriter from the command line against the src/main/java folder, using the current directory as project root, a specific model, four worker threads, exclusions, additional instructions from a file, and input logging.

features.name: Load and execute an Act
features.description: Loads a TOML-defined Act by name or absolute file path and applies it as the current workflow. The act argument supports a name plus optional prompt text. Acts can define instructions, inputs, episodes, inherited values through basedOn and $$super.value$$, default prompt values, interactive mode, path filters, model overrides, exclusions, concurrency, prologue, and epilogue.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.ActProcessor processor = new org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.ActProcessor(new java.io.File("."), "OpenAI:gpt-5.1", configurator);
processor.setAct("code-doc Update Javadoc for the public API");
examples.description: Loads the built-in code-doc act and provides prompt text that asks Ghostwriter to update Javadoc for the public API.

features.name: Guidance tag processing
features.signature: public java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.GuidanceProcessor.process(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout projectLayout, java.io.File file, java.lang.String guidance)
features.description: Composes a project-aware prompt from extracted guidance and sends it to the configured AI provider. Guidance can come from embedded @guidance comments in files or from fallback default guidance. The processor records a report for processed files and supports module-aware scanning.

examples.snippet:
<!-- @guidance:
Rewrite this Markdown page for first-time users.
Keep the language simple and include one practical example.
-->

# User Guide
examples.description: A practical Markdown guidance tag. When Ghostwriter scans the file, the Markdown reviewer extracts the guidance and uses it to update the page.

features.name: Prompt include and front matter parsing
features.description: Normalizes prompt text and resolves include lines that begin with >>>. Included content may come from file:// locations or HTTP(S) URLs and is parsed recursively. Prompt YAML front matter can override parameters such as gw.model and enabledTools for a single prompt or episode.

examples.snippet:
---
gw.model: ${public.ai.model}
enabledTools:
  - project-context
  - file-system
---
Review the implementation and apply project conventions.
>>> file://docs/coding-guidelines.md
examples.description: A prompt that keeps the ${public.ai.model} placeholder for runtime substitution, enables two tools, and includes shared coding guidelines from a project file.

features.name: Episode sequencing
features.description: Executes Act episodes in natural order from a selected starting episode while honoring repeat and move-to-episode workflow signals. Episodes allow a complex workflow to be divided into named sequential steps.

examples.description: Defines a three-episode workflow and executes it from the first episode.

features.name: Function tools for Acts
features.signature: public java.lang.Object org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.ActFunctionTools.performAct(java.lang.String actName, java.io.File projectDir, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> properties, boolean async, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator config) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Runs a named Act synchronously or asynchronously. In asynchronous mode it returns a process identifier that can later be resolved through getActResult. This enables AI workflows to launch reusable Ghostwriter tasks as tools.

examples.description: Invokes the built-in code-doc act for Java source files using a property override for the scan path.

features.name: Secure command execution
features.signature: public java.lang.Object org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools.executeCommand(java.lang.String command, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> properties, java.lang.String dir, int tailResultSize, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Executes an allowed system command in a project-relative working directory after deny-list validation. Output is captured with bounded tail retention and can be searched or paged through persisted logs. This is useful for Maven builds, tests, diagnostics, and automation steps.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools();
java.lang.Object report = tools.executeCommand("mvn test", java.util.Collections.emptyMap(), ".", 4096, "UTF-8", new java.io.File("."), configurator);
examples.description: Runs Maven tests from the project root and returns a bounded execution report.

features.name: Web and REST access
features.signature: public java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.WebFunctionTools.callRestApi(java.lang.String url, java.lang.String method, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> headers, java.lang.String body, int timeout, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Calls HTTP REST endpoints with configurable method, headers, body, timeout, charset, and Basic authentication through URL userInfo. Header values may contain ${...} placeholders that are resolved by the configurator at runtime.

examples.description: Calls a SonarQube API endpoint while preserving ${sonar.token} and ${sonar.host} placeholders for runtime configuration resolution.

customizations.name: Act TOML files
customizations.description: Custom workflows can be defined as TOML files with properties such as instructions, inputs, description, basedOn, gw.path, gw.threads, gw.excludes, gw.nonRecursive, gw.interactive, and gw.model. Acts support inheritance with basedOn and $$super.value$$, prompt placeholders such as ${public.prompt}, episode arrays, and YAML front matter for prompt-specific input parameters.

examples.snippet:
description = "Performs a project-specific review."

instructions = '''
You are a senior engineer.
'''

inputs = '''
# Task
${public.prompt}
'''

[gw]
path = "glob:src/main/java/**"
interactive = true
examples.description: A minimal custom Act that scans Java source files and runs interactively. The ${public.prompt} placeholder is intentionally preserved for runtime substitution.

customizations.name: Reviewer service-provider interface
customizations.description: Developers can add format-specific reviewers that scan files and return prompt fragments when guidance is present. Built-in reviewers support Java, Markdown, HTML/XML, Python, TypeScript, PlantUML, and @guidance.txt files.

examples.description: Shows the fully qualified Reviewer interface used to create a new file-format reviewer.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer
studs.description: Service-provider interface for components that inspect project files and extract @guidance instructions for downstream Ghostwriter processing. Implementations return a formatted prompt fragment or null when no actionable guidance is found.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer reviewer = new org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.MarkdownReviewer();
java.lang.String fragment = reviewer.perform(new java.io.File("."), new java.io.File("src/site/markdown/index.md"));
examples.description: Uses the Markdown reviewer to extract a guidance prompt fragment from a Markdown file.

examples.title: Install the Ghostwriter CLI delivery pack
examples.scenario: Use Ghostwriter as a ready-to-run command-line application.
steps: Download the Ghostwriter CLI pack from https://sourceforge.net/projects/machanism/files/machai/ghostwriter/gw.zip/download.
Unzip the archive into a tools directory such as /opt/gw or C:/tools/gw.
Ensure Java 8 or later is available on PATH by running java -version.
Configure provider credentials and Ghostwriter properties in gw.properties if required by your GenAI provider.
Run java -jar gw.jar from a project root or pass -d with the project directory.
examples.description: This scenario installs Ghostwriter as a CLI tool and verifies that the application can start.

examples.title: Process files that contain guidance tags
examples.scenario: Maintain documentation or source files using embedded @guidance comments.
examples.configuration: Add a guidance block to a Markdown file, for example: <!-- @guidance: Rewrite this page for first-time users. Keep the language simple. -->
examples.description: Ghostwriter scans the selected path, extracts guidance tags with format-specific reviewers, composes prompts, and processes the files through the configured GenAI provider.

examples.title: Run an Act workflow
examples.scenario: Execute a reusable TOML-defined automation workflow such as documentation generation or generic project assistance.
examples.configuration: Built-in acts are available by name. Custom acts can be placed in the configured gw.acts directory or supplied as an absolute TOML file path. Use ${public.prompt} in an act input template to insert the user prompt at runtime.
commands: java -jar gw.jar -a "code-doc Update Javadoc for public APIs" -d .
java -jar gw.jar -a "task Explain the purpose of this project" -d .
examples.description: Act mode loads a TOML template, merges inherited properties, applies runtime placeholders, and executes one or more prompt episodes against the project. Interactive acts accept follow-up input until the user types . to exit or > to continue.

examples.title: Use Ghostwriter in a CI/CD job
examples.scenario: Run non-interactive repository maintenance in an automated pipeline.
examples.configuration: Set gw.model, provider credentials, gw.excludes, and any required instructions in gw.properties or system properties. Keep scan targets narrow for predictable changes and review generated diffs before committing.
examples.description: This command runs Ghostwriter with a configuration file, excludes build and VCS directories, includes shared project instructions, and processes documentation files in batch mode.

examples.title: Configure a custom Act
examples.scenario: Create a reusable workflow for a team-specific code review task.
examples.configuration: Create a TOML file with instructions, inputs, and gw settings. Keep placeholders such as ${public.prompt} unchanged so they can be resolved at runtime.
examples.content:
description = "Team code review workflow."

instructions = '''
You are a senior engineer. Review for correctness, maintainability, and security.
'''

inputs = '''
# Review Task
${public.prompt}
'''

[gw]
path = "glob:src/main/java/**"
interactive = true
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to install, configure, and run a custom Act file for a real project review workflow.
